params.body:
Four defects in the photo toolbar, all found on staging on 14 September, the evening before the cutover. They are one story — the toolbar's JavaScript — so they travel together. Recorded as X-109.

## 1. A method calling its sibling on the constructor

`resources/js/vehicle/vehicle.js` is a constructor function with its methods on `vehicle.prototype`, and `app.js` hands the blades an **instance** (`window.vehicle = new Vehicle()`). Inside the module the name `vehicle` is the **constructor**, so `vehicle.verwijderTegels(...)` reaches for something that only exists on the prototype: `undefined`, and the call throws. That is Shane's `t.verwijderTegels is not a function`: the server-side delete succeeded, the callback died, the spinner kept turning and the tile stayed.

Six call sites, and I checked each against the blades rather than assuming:

| line | call | reached by |
|---|---|---|
| 23 | `if (vehicle.recolorDamageButtons) vehicle.recolorDamageButtons()` | `deleteDamage`, from `_tabs/damage.blade.php:100` — **guarded, so it failed silently** |
| 41 | `vehicle.add_months(...)` | `calculate_available_date`, bound in `ownstock/create.blade.php:445,448` and `resources/js/vehicle/create.js:50,53` |
| 46 | `vehicle.add_months(...)` | `favorite_calculate_available_date`, `onchange` in `_tabs/dates.blade.php:81,89,91,93` |
| 166 | `vehicle.recolorDamageButtons()` | `addDamage`, from `edit.blade.php:308` and `damage.blade.php:58` |
| 312 | `vehicle.verwijderTegels(images)` | `deleteSelected`, the bulk delete in both galleries |
| 342 | `vehicle.verwijderTegels([id])` | `removePhoto`, the trash can on a tile — what Shane hit |

**All six are genuinely broken in use**, not only in theory; every one sits on a path a dealer walks. Two of them deserve a word:

- **The damage buttons really do stay uncoloured today.** Line 23 is behind `if (...)`, and the guard can never be true, so after deleting the last damage at a location the diagram button never went back to grey and *nothing was logged*. Line 166 is unguarded and threw at the very end of `addDamage`'s success handler, so the damage list did update but the button never turned orange — and only a page reload fixed it. A guarded call to a method that cannot exist is not a safety net, it is a mute button. That is the lesson in the X entry.
- **The Stocklist availability date is broken, on the classic sheets.** `calculate_available_date` throws on the classic create sheet, where both the select and the date field are bound to it — so `available_on_stocklist_date` was never recomputed while creating a vehicle. `favorite_calculate_available_date` is on the classic edit sheet's Data tab, but only for a dealer with favourite dealers (`@if(filled(Auth::user()->dealer->favorite_dealers))`), so it is real but narrower. The Livewire sheet does not bind either (no `onchange` on those fields), so it was never affected.

**Shape chosen:** capture the instance at the top of the method (`var _obj = this;`) and call `_obj.<method>()`. That is the file's own shape — `duplicateSelected` and `removeBgSelected` already had `var _obj = this`, and PR 335 used exactly this to fix the same mistake in `refreshPhotos` — and unlike `this` it also works inside a jQuery `.then()`. One shape for all six. In `deleteDamage` the name `_obj` was taken by a parameter holding selectors, so that parameter is renamed `selectors` (positional, one call site, no behaviour change) rather than introducing a second capture name.

**The sibling modules are clean.** `custom.js`, `optionvalue.js`, `carpass.js`, `merchant.js`, `relation.js`, `rental.js`, `modal.js`, `access.js`, `user.js`, `structurize.js`, `location.js`, `polling.js`: **zero** genuine occurrences. The scan flags two lines in `modal.js` (12 and 15), but both are inside the header comment that documents its public API — prose about a call is not a call, and the check strips comments and strings before looking. `refreshPhotos` from PR 335 does **not** carry the mistake: it already calls `_obj.refreshPhotos(url)`.

## 2. A callback passed as a call

`vehicle.tempUpdate(form, url, after)` posts the sheet's fields to the draft and then calls `after()`. The background-removal button was written as:

```blade
onclick="vehicle.tempUpdate('…', '…', vehicle.removeBgSelected(this, '…'))"
```

so `removeBgSelected` ran **immediately** and its return value — `undefined` — was handed over as the callback. Hence `n is not a function`, and the two steps ran in the wrong order.

**Does the wrong order cause a wrong result? No, and I checked rather than assumed.** The background that gets composited is `vehicles.background_type`, read by `Photo::old_remove_background` from the vehicle row at job time. That column is written by its **own** immediate POST (`vehicle.updateBackground` → `OwnStockController::update_background_type`) at the moment the dealer clicks a swatch; the swatches are `<button type="button">`, so `tempUpdate`'s `$('input[name!=_method]', form).serialize()` never carried it in the first place. So the dealer's background choice was already saved before either request. The console error was the whole of it — but it is the same class of mistake, so it is fixed in the shape the rest of the codebase uses: `() => (vehicle.removeBgSelected(...))`.

**Every other call site was already correct.** Grepping `, vehicle.` / `, custom.` (and the other globals) inside `on*` attributes over the whole view tree returns **exactly one** hit: this line. The other four `tempUpdate` sites (`photos.blade.php` ×2, `photos/stocklist.blade.php` ×2) and `ducplicateImage` in `photos/image.blade.php` all pass a real function.

*Noted, not changed:* `tempUpdate` calls `after()` only from `.then()`'s success branch, so if the draft save itself fails the second step silently never runs. Out of scope here.

## 3. The label that lied

"achtergrond verwijderen bij alle foto's" acted on the checked photos. The swap between `photos.remove_bg_all` and `photos.remove_bg_selected` lived as jQuery in the **classic** sheets only (`create.blade.php` ~401, `edit.blade.php` ~465), and the Livewire sheet includes the partial but not that script — so the label was frozen on "alle" while the action followed the selection.

Fixed in the partial, driven by state that was already there: the toolbar's Alpine component counts the selection in `sel` (checked `.image_checkbox` inside its own root, which is the own-offer gallery — the platform gallery has its own scope and its own `image_stocklist_checkbox`), so the label follows it with `x-text`. The classic jQuery swap is **removed** from both classic sheets: it drove the same two spans, and two mechanisms fighting over one span is worse than one. Both sheets verified in the browser.

The swap covered **both** batch buttons, so the duplicate button gets the same treatment — doing only one would have left half the toolbar on the old mechanism.

**What the button does with nothing checked:** it acts on **all** photos — `removeBgSelected` falls back to every `.image_checkbox` when none is checked, and the server then skips the ones already processed (`trans_path`/`processed_uuid` not null). So "bij alle foto's" is *true* in that state, and "bij geselecteerde foto's" is true in the other. The label now states both truthfully; the id `removebg_selected` is a misnomer but is left alone (it is the hook the CSS and the tests use).

## 4. The bulk 504

Verified the chain before touching it: both bulk buttons collected every id and sent **one** request; `OwnStockController::removeBgImages` / `ImageController::duplicate_image` loop over the list and `ProcessImage::dispatch()` each one; outside production `Outbound::seal()` sets `queue.default` to `sync`, so every dispatch runs **inline** — eighteen round trips to remove.bg or Blurit inside a single HTTP request, and the gateway gives up at thirty seconds.

Now one request per photo, a few in flight, each tile carrying its own spinner: `perFoto(ids, verzoek, klaar)` on the prototype. The endpoints are untouched (they still take a list; it now has one entry in it), so the partner API and the classic sheets see no change beyond the call shape. `refreshPhotos` runs **once at the end**, not per photo.

**Concurrency is 3.** Low enough not to occupy the handful of PHP-FPM workers a Forge site has (a dealer holding the tab open must not starve the rest of the site, and on staging the queue is inline so each request holds a worker for its full external call), low enough not to get throttled by remove.bg, and high enough that eighteen photos do not become eighteen serial waits. It is a constant in one place if it needs tuning.

**Failures are reported honestly.** `meldBatch(total, failed)` sends the usual "being processed" notice only when nothing failed; otherwise `ui.notify` says how many of how many failed, in red (`ui.photos_batch_failed`, added in all five locales and exposed through `slTeksten`). Reporting success for a half-failed batch would be the same silence as the guarded call above.

**This does not remove the need for a queue worker on production.** The automatic platform copies added in PR 334 dispatch jobs from the save path, so without a worker those still run inline in the request that saves a shared vehicle.

## The check that now catches this

`tests/Feature/HandlerWiringTest.php`, in the shape of `AlpineExpressionTest` / `BuildContractTest`:

1. **`test_no_module_calls_its_own_prototype_method_on_the_constructor`** — for every module with a `X.prototype = { ... }` object, any `X.<method>(` where `<method>` is on that prototype. Comments and string literals are blanked first (keeping line and column positions) so `modal.js`'s API comment does not read as code. Run over the whole tree: after this PR, zero hits; nothing had to be narrowed away or excluded.
2. **`test_no_inline_handler_passes_a_call_where_a_function_belongs`** — in any `on*="…"` attribute, an argument that is itself a call to one of the globals. Over the whole view tree this flags exactly the broken shape and nothing else; it is deliberately not narrowed to a list of callback-taking helpers, because narrowing would be the thing that lets the next one through.

Both were mutation-checked: reverting one self-call (including back to the **guarded** form, which the check still catches) and reverting the callback each make the suite fail with the file and line.

## Verified in a running application

Not only in tests — a running app is the only thing that would have caught any of this. Local server, own MySQL database built from `database/schema/mysql-schema.sql` plus the post-2026-07-28 migrations as CI does, a seeded dealer with 18 photos, console open:

- **Deleting a photo**: the tile disappears, the spinner stops, **0 console errors**. `photo-delete-works.png`
- **Label**: "bij alle foto's" with nothing checked, "bij geselecteerde foto's" the moment one is — same for the duplicate button. `label-follows-selection.png`
- **18 photos duplicated**: 18 separate `POST /image/{id}/duplicate` in the server log, none long enough to time out, the gallery refreshed once at the end, 0 console errors.
- **Partial failure**: with the server down mid-batch, "17 van de 17 foto's zijn niet gelukt. Probeer die opnieuw." in red instead of a cheerful "wordt verwerkt". `batch-failure-is-reported.png`

`npm run build` succeeds and the app chunk stays import/export-free (`BuildContractTest` green). Full suite: **733 tests, 732 pass**, the only failure being `BuildStampTest`, which is the known worktree artifact (it reads the build stamp from the checkout).
params.title: Deleting a photo left the spinner running
